ELI5: Why does my singing voice sound perfect in my head, but when I'm singing out loud, I sound terrible?

Your head imagines a sound but your body isn't able to reproduce that sound, therefore sounding terrible. Professional singers practice to reach that desired sound so they can replicate the voice they hear in their head.
because you make the sound in your throat/lungs not your head. think from those locations.

I believe it is because when you hear yourself speak/sing, you're also hearing the sound reverberating from the inside of your head. So it sound different to you than it would to people around you. If you've ever been in an extremely confined place you'd notice the same type of effect. The only example I can think of is if you've ever been in a pool with a blowup raft or flotation device with a bottom to it, turn it upside down, swim under and stick your head in. Start talking and you'll you will sound different than normal
If you practice with a microphone and monitor you will improve rapidly.

I browsed /r/mensrights about two years ago. I saw the FAQ that listed their concerns and contained explanations with sources. The clear, easy to understand post helped me empathize. My understanding of feminism had been formed largely by reddit and youtube, and all I really knew was it empowered women, got them the right to vote . Like most people, I'm not exactly a fan of censorship, so the sight of /r/shitredditsays was rather unsettling: lots of sarcasm and vitriol, and not much discussion as far as I could tell. I saw posts about "SJWs" and it was hard for me to empathize. Women can get jobs and vote, after all.

Recently, I've adopted the feminist label. I considered how many intelligent people I know (irl) who call themselves such and realized there must be something there. So I did some homework and came out seeing the other side of the sexism coin. The side that is approximately 100x as large. Since then, I have been active on /v/feminism and I still have much to learn.

/v/feminism is a little less than 1/10th the size of /v/mensrights, if that tells you anything about the state of this site. Even on /v/feminism I frequently get responses that are in total denial of feminist issues (including gender roles or their consequences, even when there are plenty of complaints about gender roles and their effects on /v/mensrights (talk about hypocrisy)) or try to change the subject by talking about how bad men have it.

Elsewhere on this site, sexist comments are twice as common and four times as ugly. I thought maybe there is a place I can archive this drivel, and I don't want it to be /v/feminism. This seems like the place, but my concerns are 1) the sarcasm, which I see as circlejerking and 2) the "not a place for debate" rule. I came to where I am today by understanding the issues, not being exposed to caustic comments. Is there an archive for "shit voaters say" that does allow for discussion and maybe doesn't have so much sarcasm? The way to win people is through education. I had to see the light before I saw the shit.

My plea today is two-fold. Let us make feminist issues easier to understand for outsiders and come visit us at /v/feminism and contribute!
